excerpts.content:
I found this log on Witti:

```
May 26 21:27:45.526 WARN Found peer during discovery not on correct fork, tcp_socket: 92.200.29.16:13000, our_enr: Ok(EnrForkId { fork_digest: [246, 119, 93, 7], next_fork_version: [0, 0, 1, 19], next_fork_epoch: Epoch(18446744073709551615) }), their_enr: Ok(EnrForkId { fork_digest: [246, 119, 93, 7], next_fork_version: [0, 0, 0, 0], next_fork_epoch: Epoch(18446744073709551615) }), peer_id: QmQ8SRg3XmzLvEDvaLgDYKPbmqEDtTGF5Bkd7QCkhBVsbB, service: libp2p
```

What this says is there's someone who is declaring the same `fork_digest` as us, but not declaring the same `next_fork_version`. This means that we agree on `current_fork_version` and `genesis_validators_root`, but not on `next_fork_version`. The simplest answer I can think for this is that some client (whoever uses 13000) is setting their `next_fork_version` to "default" (all zeros) instead of equal to `current_fork_version`, like the spec says.
